questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Mileage information, such as distances to specific locations.

questions.explanation: Blue signs tell you about services available ahead. They show where to find rest areas, food, gas, hospitals, and other help.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Round yellow signs warn you of railroad crossings ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic from another lane may merge into your lane ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Round signs mean a railroad crossing is ahead. The sign is placed a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn about hazards ahead. Round signs are used only for railroad crossings.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped yellow signs warn of danger ahead. Orange diamond signs warn about hazards in or near construction areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop. Wait until the way is clear before you safely proceed through the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it travels slowly. You see this on farm equipment, road work vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons. It appears solid orange during the day and hollow red at night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop and yield to pedestrians and cross traffic.
Slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and yield to pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at the marked stop line or before the crosswalk or intersection. Let other vehicles and pedestrians pass if they are in your path. Then you may proceed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings are warning signs. This sign warns that another road crosses ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to what is ahead. This sign warns that your road ends at an intersection. Slow down and prepare to yield or stop before turning right or left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: May turn left only on a green arrow.
May turn left on a green light when it is safe.
Must wait for the solid green light before you turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn left on a green light when it is safe.
questions.explanation: "Yield" means slow down and be ready to stop for vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians. After you yield, you can follow the rest of the sign's instructions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed. You may see this sign where traffic comes from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn can be made here.
A left turn can be made only after stopping.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn can be made here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means left turns are prohibited here.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You may proceed if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road. If you see this sign while driving, traffic is moving toward you. Turn around and do not proceed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead winds with a series of turns or curves.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers that the road becomes slippery when wet. Drive carefully in wet conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs indicate construction ahead. Proceed with caution.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign means right turns are not allowed where it is posted. You must obey this sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always sound your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This five-sided sign alerts you to a school zone. Be alert for children and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Proceed at a consistent speed while looking and listening for approaching trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for any trains, and be prepared to stop if any trains are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for any trains, and be prepared to stop if any trains are nearby.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains and be ready to stop if one approaches. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and do not use your brakes.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead becomes slippery when wet. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are approaching you.
Come to a full stop then proceed when it is safe to do so.
Proceed carefully through the intersection, not always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop then proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign means stop. Come to a complete stop at the marked line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk or intersection. Only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers to watch for pedestrians crossing the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you that traffic signals are ahead at an intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School zone or school crossing sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing sign.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns of a school zone. It alerts drivers that children may be crossing in this area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is posted on one-way streets and roadways where you cannot enter. Do not proceed in this direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet. Drive with caution.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and yield to traffic on the main road when merging.
Always come to a complete stop.
Activate your turn signal and proceed into traffic at the usual speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to traffic on the main road when merging.
questions.explanation: A three-sided yield sign means you must let other vehicles pass before you proceed. Slow down and enter the intersection carefully. You do not always need to stop, but you must be ready to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right turns permitted on a red light.

questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns. Do not turn right where this sign is posted.
